titulo: Introductions, countries, numbers 0 to 20 and age: Greetings and introductions

aula.titulo: Introductions, countries, numbers 0 to 20 and age
aula.objetivo: Introduce yourself and others, name countries and nationalities, count from 0 to 20 and say your age with «avere». Choose between «tu» and «Lei», and avoid the three classic English-speaker traps: «sono bene», «sono venti anni» and a capital letter on nationalities.

blocos.contexto: Signora Rossi meets Ana at a course, and then Marco joins them. Listen once without reading. Notice that nobody says «is» or «name»: the Italian for «What is your name?» is built on a different verb.

linhas.ru: — Buongiorno, mi chiamo Elena Rossi. Come si chiama?
linhas.pt: — Good morning, my name is Elena Rossi. What is your name?
linhas.audio: Buongiorno, mi chiamo Elena Rossi. Come si chiama?

linhas.ru: — Buongiorno, signora. Mi chiamo Ana. Piacere.
linhas.pt: — Good morning, madam. My name is Ana. Pleased to meet you.
linhas.audio: Buongiorno, signora. Mi chiamo Ana. Piacere.

linhas.pt: — Pleased to meet you, Ana. How are you?
— I'm fine, thank you. And you?

linhas.ru: — Molto bene, grazie. Questo è Marco.
linhas.pt: — Very well, thank you. This is Marco.
linhas.audio: Molto bene, grazie. Questo è Marco.

linhas.pt: — Good morning, Ana. Pleased to meet you.

itens.pt: my name is (literally: I call myself)
what is your name? (to a friend)
what is your name? (to a stranger)
this is (a man or a masculine thing)
this is (a woman or a feminine thing)

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Italian does not say «my name is». It says «mi chiamo», which is literally «I call myself». STEP 2: the question follows the same logic: «Come ti chiami?» is literally «How do you call yourself?». There is no «is», no «your» and no word for «name». STEP 3: «mi» and «ti» are the small words that carry «myself» and «yourself». Without them the verb changes meaning: «chiamo» alone means «I call» someone, as in «I call a taxi». STEP 4: to answer, say «Mi chiamo» and your name, with no pronoun: «Mi chiamo Ana.» The word «io» is not needed, because the verb ending already tells you who is speaking. STEP 5: the stress falls on the middle syllable: «mee KYAH-moh». The «chi» is a hard «k»: «kya», as in «keen», not «chee».
blocos.comparacao: English has a fixed frame: «My name is ___» and «What is your name?». Italian has no «name» and no «is» in either sentence. Do not translate word by word: learn «Mi chiamo…» and «Come ti chiami?» as two blocks. English speakers also tend to say «chi» like «chee» (as in «cheese»), but in «chiami» it is «kya».

exemplos.pt: What is your name? (to a friend)

tabela.exemplo: My name is Ana.  /  What is your name?
Mi chiamo Ana.  /  Come ti chiami?

erros.motivo: Without «mi», «chiamo» means «I call (someone)». The «mi» is the «myself».
A word-for-word copy of «What is your name?» is understood, but it sounds like a textbook. Use «Come ti chiami?».

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: English has one «you» for everybody. Italian chooses between two forms, depending on the relationship. STEP 2: use the informal form («tu») with friends, family, children and people your own age in a relaxed setting: «Come ti chiami?», «Come stai?». STEP 3: use the formal form («Lei») with strangers, older people, and in shops, offices and hotels: «Come si chiama?», «Come sta?». STEP 4: with «Lei» the verb takes the form you would use for «she», and «Lei» is often written with a capital letter when it means «you»: «E Lei?». STEP 5: when in doubt, start formal. Italians will invite you to use «tu» when they are ready. STEP 6: «Piacere» is what you say when you meet someone: it means «pleased to meet you». It is not «please»; for «please» Italian says «per favore». STEP 7: «Sto bene» means «I am well». Use «stare» for how you feel, not «essere»: «Sto bene», not «Sono bene».
blocos.comparacao: English «you» hides the difference that Italian makes visible, so the choice feels new. A useful parallel is the English jump between «Hey, how are you?» and «Good morning, madam, how do you do?»: Italian puts that switch into the grammar. Also watch the false friend «piacere»: it looks like «pleasure» and works as «pleased to meet you», but it never means «please».

erros.motivo: A stranger you call «signora» gets the formal form.
Health and mood use «stare», not «essere». English «I am well» is the trap.
«Piacere» already means «pleased to meet you»; it is not «please».

itens.explicacao: «Piacere» is what you say on meeting someone. «Per favore» is the real «please».
Listen to the first sound: «mi» is «I», while «ti» would be «you».

itens.enunciado: Which sentence do you say to a stranger you call «signora»?
itens.explicacao: «Si chiama» is the formal form, used with «Lei».
Use «stare»: «Sto bene». English «I am well» does not become «sono bene».

itens.enunciado: What does «Piacere» mean when you meet someone?
itens.explicacao: It looks like «please», but «please» is «per favore».
Short and formal: there is no «your» and no «name» in Italian.

blocos.enunciado: Introduce yourself out loud as if you were meeting a stranger and then a friend: «Buongiorno, mi chiamo… Piacere.» Then ask the friend: «Come ti chiami?»
Say the two questions for «What is your name?», formal and informal, and explain to yourself why neither contains the word «name».
